title: Estimating Individualized Causal Effect with Confounded Instruments

problem.claim: Estimating individualized causal effects is difficult when unmeasured confounders are present.

gap.claim: Existing instrument-variable methods depend on valid instruments satisfying an untestable unconfounded instruments assumption, making valid-instrument discovery difficult.

contributions.claim: CVAE-IV uses a conditional variational autoencoder to generate a substitute for an unmeasured confounder from confounded instruments and their conditional independence with the outcome.
The method provides a theoretical guarantee that the generated confounder substitute identifies unbiased individualized causal effects.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CVAE-IV as a novel method for estimating individualized causal effects with confounded instruments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on bias demand prediction and Mendelian randomization analysis verify the effectiveness of CVAE-IV.

narrative_sequence.summary: Individualized causal-effect learning supports fine-grained policy evaluation and personalized treatment development.
Unmeasured confounders make individualized causal-effect estimation difficult, while existing instrument-variable approaches require untestable assumptions about instrument validity.
The paper addresses confounded instruments by using a conditional variational autoencoder to generate a substitute for the unmeasured confounder.
The authors report a guarantee that the generated substitute identifies unbiased individualized causal effects.
The authors report effectiveness in bias demand prediction and Mendelian randomization analysis.

source_observation.claim: The method uses conditional independence between confounded instruments and the outcome to generate a substitute for an unmeasured confounder.

interpretation.claim: When standard instrument validity is unavailable, observable conditional-independence structure may support construction of a latent-confounder proxy.

application.claim: Consider latent-confounder substitution methods in individualized causal-effect estimation with confounded instruments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the required conditional-independence condition holds in a given application.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal assumptions or conditions underlying the theoretical guarantee.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
